items.text: Hydrogen is the most common element in the universe.

items.label: text
items.text: The melting point and boiling point of hydrogen are shown in the table:

items.label: list_item
items.text: a Put a cross in the box to show a temperature at which hydrogen is a liquid.

items.label: list_item
items.text: b The circle in the diagram represents 1 molecule of hydrogen. Complete the diagram to show the arrangement of particles in liquid hydrogen. You should add at least 10 more circles to the diagram.

items.label: list_item
items.text: c Hydrogen has three isotopes, the least common of which is tritium, ³H. Use the Periodic Table to work out the number of protons, neutrons and electrons in an atom of tritium. (ε)

items.label: list_item
items.text: d Hydrogen reacts with nitrogen to form ammonia (NH₃).

items.text: i The electronic configuration of a nitrogen atom is (put a cross in one :(xoq

items.label: list_item
items.text: ii Draw a dot-and-cross diagram, showing outer electrons only, to show the bonding in an ammonia molecule.

items.label: list_item
items.text: e Ammonia forms salts that contain the ammonium ion. Put a cross in the box to show which of the following formulae for ammonium compounds is incorrect.
